use_case_name: Publish Air and Surface Surveillance Tracks

claims.content: To publish air and surface surveillance tracks with automatic decorrelation capability, and to perform common tracking defined as sharing of a common track number and shifting R² between C² JUs.

scope_contract.goal_statement: To publish air and surface surveillance tracks with automatic decorrelation capability, and to perform common tracking defined as sharing of a common track number and shifting R² between C² JUs.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: A C2 JU initiates a real-time air or surface track, automatically decorrelates it, and publishes it as a common track using a shared common track number, thereby enabling R² shifting between C² JUs.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The C2 JU has a real-time air or surface track to initiate/publish.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The air or surface track is published with automatic decorrelation under a shared common track number, with R² shifting between C² JUs supported.
in_scope_actions: Publish an air or surface surveillance track
Support R² shifting between C² JUs
excluded_adjacent_actions: Executing the physical R² handoff after publication
variant_dimensions: Single C2 JU initiating vs. multiple C2 JUs sharing the track

claims.content: C2 JU
The C2 JU must have initially achieved Active status, or returned to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure.
The C2 JU must be capable of assuming R² for air or surface tracks.
The C2 JU must have an automatic decorrelation capability for real-time air or surface tracks it initiates.
A C2 JU initiates a real-time air or surface track.
The C2 JU initiates a real-time air or surface track.

After achieving Active status, or after returning to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure, the C2 JU completes sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration before transmitting the track.
The C2 JU applies the minimum 12-second wait before reporting the air or surface track.
The C2 JU compares locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with the data received on the interface.

The C2 JU does not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates any of the following: an Identity difference constituting a conflict; different Mode II codes while the local Mode II code is current; both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks; or either track has a Strength field greater than 1.
The C2 JU performs automatic decorrelation tests for each common local track upon receipt of each J2 or J3 message on the track.

The C2 JU decorrelates the common local track if, on receipt of 2(1-5,1) consecutive remote track reports, the remote track falls outside a distance of 1.5(1.0-2.0,0.1) times the maximum correlation distance.
After decorrelation is determined, the C2 JU automatically tests the local track once for correlation against remote tracks, not common local tracks.
If the automatic correlation test fails, the C2 JU assigns a new track number (TN B) to the local track and reports TN B in a J3.2 or J3.3 message with an initial ID of Pending.
The C2 JU establishes the previous track number (TN A) as a remote track.
Diverges from Step 2: If an operator action has been taken that selectively released a new local track for reporting, the C2 JU transmits the track regardless of the results of correlation testing.

Diverges from Step 4: If the locally held Environment/Category of a track differs from that received in a J3.X or J7.0 (ACT=1) message, the C2 JU alerts the operator, even if the received Environment/Category is not implemented.
Diverges from Step 5: If an ID difference cannot be automatically accepted or rejected, the C2 JU presents the ID differences to operators for evaluation; resolution may require voice coordination.
Diverges from Step 5: If the ID conflict is resolved, the C2 JU tests the track number to be retained for decorrelation once before executing the correlation.
Diverges from Step 7: The C2 JU may perform manual decorrelation, and may be configured to require manual confirmation before an automatic decorrelation is executed.

Diverges from Step 7: If track number TN A is controlled by the C2 JU's own unit (subject of a J10.5 Controlling Unit Report message), the C2 JU does not automatically decorrelate; if the operator manually decorrelates, the C2 JU alerts the operator to report termination of control on TN A if appropriate, and reports commencement of control of TN B via J10.5 only if initiated by operator action.

Diverges from Step 7: If track number TN A has been paired by the C2 JU's own unit (subject of a J10.6 message), the C2 JU decorrelates and alerts an operator as a cue to terminate the pairing on TN A and initiate the pairing on TN B if appropriate.

Diverges from Step 8: As a system option, the C2 JU may include common local tracks in the automatic correlation tests performed upon receipt of remote real-time messages or prior to transmission of a local track.

Diverges from Step 2: If a dual designation has occurred (which can result from failure to properly correlate local track data with respect to remote data) and the C2 JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, the C2 JU initiates action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.

Diverges from Step 4: If the C2 JU is a JU without R² and receives a J3 or J7.5 (ACT=1) message with remote IFF/SIF data differing from locally held data, it responds according to Table 4.7-5; when the operator receives the resulting IFF/SIF data conflict alert, the C2 JU provides the manual resolution options: update local data manually or verify automatic inputs; initiate J7.5 (ACT=0) Clear IFF/SIF; initiate J7.5 (ACT=1) IFF/SIF Difference Report; change local data to agree with remote data except in the case of Mode II code; decorrelate the local data from the remote data, causing assignment of a new track number to local data; or clear the operator alert. Exit: the branch completes when the operator takes one of the listed resolution actions.
Diverges from Step 5: If either track has its Strength field set to 'No Statement', the restriction on automatic correlation based on Strength values does not apply.

Diverges from Step 8: If the Retained TN and the Dropped TN would decorrelate when subjected to the decorrelation criteria once, the correlation shall be rejected. Exit: the correlation request is rejected.

Diverges from Step 8: If the C2 JU receives a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3, it automatically accepts the requested correlation unless one of the following restrictions applies: different Environment/Category or existing E/C conflict; one simulated and one live track; or both locally derived real-time tracks. If a restriction applies, the correlation shall be rejected. Exit: if a restriction applies, the correlation is rejected; otherwise the correlation is accepted.

Diverges from Step 8: When a correlation request is rejected for manual correlation, the C2 JU that originated the request provides an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination. Exit: the operator alert is provided.
Diverges from Step 2: If the C2 JU has not received a remote report on a locally held Air or Surface (Maritime) track for approximately 40 seconds, it assumes R² for that track. Exit: R² is assumed.

Diverges from Step 2: If the C2 JU receives a J7.0 (ACT=0) message on a locally held track, the R² unit is declared inactive; the C2 JU shall assume R² at the next opportunity to transmit the track if local reporting eligibility remains and a remote report has not been received on that track. Exit: R² is assumed at that next transmission opportunity.

Diverges from Step 2: If the C2 JU receives a J2 PPLI message with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive, Conditional Radio Silence, or TDS Failure from a JU that has R² of a locally held track, it may assume R² at the next opportunity to transmit the track if local reporting eligibility remains and a remote report has not been received on that track. Exit: R² may be assumed at that next transmission opportunity.

Explicit continuation of the publication flow after an IFF/SIF conflict resolution action is taken

Evidence does not explicitly state 'and the C2 JU does not reject the correlation on that basis' nor the exit condition 'continue evaluating the remaining correlation restrictions at Step 5'.

claims.content: The new local track is transmitted when no tentative correlation is found on the initial test, when it tentatively correlates on the initial test but fails correlation on the next test, or when an operator has selectively released it for reporting (the latter regardless of correlation testing results).
A new local track that correlates with another track on each of the first two correlation tests is correlated and held as a common local track.
Thereafter, the decorrelation rules apply to the common local track.
After successful decorrelation execution (automatic or manual), the original local track (TN A) is established as a remote track.
If the automatic correlation test fails during decorrelation, the system assigns a new track number (TN B) to the local track and reports TN B in a J3.2 or J3.3 message with an initial ID of Pending.
